content:
I have a bunch of 2D shape types, each of which has a to_json : ... -> Try(Str, _) method.

I'd like to also have a List of these shapes so I've created a type:

Shape := [
  Arc(Arc),
  Line(Line),
  Square(Square),
  ...
]

my_shapes : List(Shape)
...

And I'd like to be able to serialize the whole list to a JSON array of structs/lists but I can see there's going to be problems with the "outer" and "inner" JSON components of the list of shapes.

Is this something where encoder_for() is relevant? Has anyone done something similar I can look at?
I'm not sure, but for use cases beyond the builtin Json I have been using https://lukewilliamboswell.github.io/roc-parser/#json

FWIW I ended up adding a record type to each shape module suitable for JSON or other export then the to_json() function can become:

to_json : Polyline -> Try(Str, _)
to_json = |shape| {
  Json.to_str_try(Polyline(shape.to_record()))
}
